The test image shows a mango leaf with **discrete dark brown/black spots** scattered across the leaf surface. The spots are irregular in shape, somewhat angular, and appear sunken or necrotic. The rest of the leaf is green and healthy-looking. No white powder, no sooty coating, no tip/margin dieback.

This pattern — discrete dark necrotic lesions on otherwise green tissue — is classic for **Anthracnose**.

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference Anthracnose image shows a severely affected/yellowed leaf — different stage than the test image. However, re-assessing based on visual features:

**Test image features:**
- Green leaf with discrete dark brown/black necrotic spots
- Spots are irregular, scattered, somewhat angular
- No white coating → rules out Powdery_Mildew
- No uniform sooty layer → rules out Sooty_Mould  
- No tip/margin dieback pattern → rules out Die_Back
- Discrete lesions on green tissue → consistent with **Anthracnose** (early/mid stage)

The discrete dark fungal lesions on otherwise healthy green tissue is the textbook presentation of Anthracnose, even if the reference I viewed showed a more advanced case.
